For differentiable convex $g$, the supporting-line inequality is $g(x)\ge g(m)+g'(m)(x-m)$ at $m=\mathbb E[X]$. Taking expectations cancels the linear term, giving Jensen's inequality. Subgradients extend the argument to suitable nondifferentiable convex functions. Concave $\log$ reverses the inequality. [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

Write $\log p_\theta(x)=\log\mathbb E_{q_\phi(z|x)}[p_\theta(x,z)/q_\phi(z|x)]$. Applying concavity yields $\mathbb E_q[\log p_\theta(x,z)-\log q_\phi(z|x)]$, which expands into the expected reconstruction log likelihood minus $D_{KL}(q_\phi(z|x)\|p(z))$. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114)

The gap is $D_{KL}(q_\phi(z|x)\|p_\theta(z|x))\ge0$. Equality holds when the variational posterior equals the true posterior, subject to support and integrability requirements. Optimizing the bound jointly improves the generative model and its approximate posterior; a restricted variational family can leave a nonzero inference gap.
